clue.text: Duenna takes in art master as interpreter

indicators.note: to take in a guest is to hold them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce chaperone, which is what a duenna is
an MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A chaperone brings an art teacher along to translate for her charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The MA goes between the O and the N at the end of the fierce chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was a guide and translator in Turkish, Arabic and Persian speaking countries.

clue.text: Take part in practice

definitions.note: read as go through a part, an actor's role
definitions.meaning: first meaning: go over an actor's role before the performance

definitions.note: the verb, in the spelling used outside Britain
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to train or drill something repeatedly

explanation.surface: Join in with a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take part' sounds like participate, but a part here is an actor's role, which you take through its paces before opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over a play or piece repeatedly in preparation is the standard meaning, so it means both drilling and running through a role.

clue.text: Philosopher takes Jane to the old mountain

parts.note: William Godwin, the English political philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher escorts Jane on an outing to some ancient hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Godwin was the father of Mary Shelley; the Jane is the author of Pride and Prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Godwin-Austen was the former official name of K2, the world's second highest peak.

clue.text: Curses girl for interrupting writer's work

indicators.note: someone interrupting barges into the middle, so this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, what a writer produces

explanation.surface: Someone swears because a girl keeps breaking in on an author at work.
explanation.walkthrough: ALISON sits between the M and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a malediction, the opposite of benison or blessing.

clue.text: Book to see actor

parts.note: a novel is a kind of book
lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: Read the book in order to meet the star.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh actor, composer and matinee idol of the 1920s and 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was famous on stage and in films as a romantic leading performer.

clue.text: Buy it back? Think again!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: recover something by paying, as from a pawnbroker
second meaning, split as RE plus DEEM: to deem or judge once more

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning only works if the word is read in two parts, a prefix meaning again and a verb meaning think.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering a pawned item by payment is the plain sense; to deem is to consider or judge.

clue.text: Miss Verity losing her head?

definitions.note: a girl's name standing for a Miss

indicators.note: a head is the top of a word written downward, so its first letter is lost

parts.note: verity means truth; it is also a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young lady named Verity seems to have lost her composure.
explanation.walkthrough: Verity looks like the girl here, but she is the source word; the girl is the result once T goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a girl's name, so it can be a Miss, an unmarried young woman addressed by title.

clue.text: Retaliation concerning Paris trip, may conclude

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters before it fall into a new order

parts.note: the printed clue has no word that ends in this letter; the original probably read 'all conclude', the last of all

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a Paris trip may end in revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed seems garbled: RE plus a rearrangement of PARIS needs one more L, which no word here supplies cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation, paying back an injury with another.

clue.text: Proposal is noted?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an opening approach or offer

definitions.note: cryptic: a piece that is written in musical notes
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the orchestral opening of an opera, set down in notes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' seems to mean remarked on, but the question mark hints at musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is both a tentative offer made to start negotiations and an instrumental introduction to an opera.

clue.text: Such a deep part of the lake!

indicators.note: only a part of the words before it is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how deep one stretch of a lake is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts in the middle of Such and ends at the start of deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Chad is a large, famously shallow lake in central Africa, which makes the surface ironic.

clue.text: Come safely through without strike, eh? That's lucky

definitions.note: a description of the answer, standing for something considered lucky

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to weather a storm is to come through it safely

explanation.surface: Getting through without an industrial strike would be lucky, wouldn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without strike' looks like 'with no strike', but without is used in its old sense of outside, so the weathering phrase goes around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig of white heather is a traditional Scottish charm for good fortune, often given to brides.

clue.text: Sport occupies four nights — it appears wrong

indicators.note: if the order looks wrong it must be put right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some pastime takes up four nights, and something seems amiss about that.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling for trout with rod and line is a popular field sport, especially fly fishing.

clue.text: Rob irregular soldier of horse

indicators.note: irregular means not in the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a non-commissioned officer, such as a corporal or sergeant

explanation.surface: Steal an irregular fighter's mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular soldier' reads as a guerrilla, but irregular goes back to Rob and the soldier is plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an untamed or half-broken horse of the American West.

clue.text: Current content of divers satires

indicators.note: the content of a box is what sits inside it, so one piece fills the other

parts.note: loons are diving birds, called divers in Britain
an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: The current issue holds a variety of satirical pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like the old word for various, but these divers are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a sharp piece of writing that ridicules a person, a kind of satire.

clue.text: There's some point in backing issues for Moslems

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from the end
in places one piece inside another

parts.note: north is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone says there is some sense in supporting the concerns of Muslims.
explanation.walkthrough: The backwards SEUSSI takes N after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senussi are a Sufi Muslim order and brotherhood based in Libya and the Sahara.

clue.text: Employees take the ring road in town

explanation.surface: Workers use the ring road when driving through town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is a market town in the English Midlands, the administrative centre of its county.

clue.text: After talk, permitted return of property

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in order
to return is to go back, so the word is read from its end

explanation.surface: After discussion, the owner was allowed to have her belongings back.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal property, as opposed to land or buildings.

clue.text: A garden farewell to un toothsome creatures

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to a garden of unappetising animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'un toothsome' as without teeth rather than unappetising.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is the old zoological order of toothless mammals, such as anteaters, sloths and armadillos.

clue.text: Gamble about girl upsetting the title

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
to upset is to turn over, which in a down entry flips the word end to end

explanation.surface: A wager about a young woman unsettles the title holder.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, upsetting turns a word upside down, which reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title ranking below a baron and above a knight.

clue.text: Nymph is heart-broken' — goes to country

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heartbroken nymph leaves for another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-broken' reads as one sad word; split it and the heart is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Arethusa was a nymph changed into a spring to escape the river god Alpheus.

clue.text: Mysteriously haunts French island

indicators.note: something done mysteriously is done in a strange, unexplained way, so the letters become jumbled

explanation.surface: Something ghostly frequents an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushant, Ouessant in French, is the island off Brittany marking the entrance to the English Channel.

clue.text: Notts opener wasn't well caught

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the start of the word is kept

parts.note: Notts is short for Nottinghamshire, an English cricket county
to be ill is to ail

explanation.surface: The Nottinghamshire opening batsman was ill and got out caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' looks like a cricket batsman, but it selects a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a suspect is informal for catching or arresting them.

clue.text: Shine in languages

explanation.surface: Someone excels at foreign tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shine in languages' reads as being good at them; the plural word supplies two different tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a glossy shellac finish for fine wood furniture, giving it a high lustre.

clue.text: Poetry has no opening in this tongue

indicators.note: without an opening the word lacks its start, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: Poetry in this language starts with no opening line.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: State gets cowards confession?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a country in the Middle East

definitions.note: cryptic: what a coward would admit to
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split as two words: a coward admits to having fled

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, to declare, which fits the confession; it is the noun, a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, formerly Persia, so it is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Peer's son gives wrong answer

indicators.note: a wrong order must be corrected, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A nobleman's son replies incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply, something said or written back to a question.

clue.text: Message from the border — permitted to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the whole string is read from its end

parts.note: marge is a poetic word for margin or edge

explanation.surface: A wire comes from the frontier, allowed to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces together, not just the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph and delivered in printed form.
